extracted.intended_audience: developers, repository collaborators and repository administrators using GitHub
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing and requesting code reviews on GitHub pull requests, including review actions, who may review, requesting reviewers, and enforcing required approvals before merge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of pull request reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborate on pull requests to improve code quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers can comment on changes, suggest improvements, and approve or request changes before code is merged. This collaborative process enables teams to ensure code quality and share knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone with read access can review and comment on proposed changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repository owners and collaborators can request reviews from specific people or teams. When you define code owners in a CODEOWNERS file, they're automatically requested as reviewers when a pull request modifies their code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review status — Comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment: Share feedback without approving or requesting changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this status to provide observations, questions, or non-blocking suggestions. Comments appear in the conversation timeline and merge box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review status — Approve
rubrics_metrics.description: Approve: Approve the changes for merging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Approve to signal that the changes are acceptable and the PR can be merged (subject to any other repository rules). Approvals are shown in the review timeline and merge box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review status — Request changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Request changes: Identify issues that must be fixed before merging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this status to block merging until the author addresses the identified problems. Provide actionable information about what must be changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line-level comments and suggested changes
rubrics_metrics.description: You can comment on specific lines and suggest changes for authors to apply directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use inline comments to point to exact places in the diff; use suggested changes to provide ready-to-apply edits. This helps authors make precise updates and speeds up iteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion of implementation approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss implementation approaches within the review conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the conversation timeline to debate design choices, tradeoffs, and alternatives so reviewers and authors can converge on an approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking addressed feedback by resolving threads
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark conversation threads as resolved to track addressed feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolving threads documents which feedback has been handled and clarifies remaining open issues for reviewers and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting and re-requesting reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Repository owners and collaborators can request reviews from specific people or teams; you can re-request reviews after making significant changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CODEOWNERS entries cause automatic reviewer requests when their code is modified. Re-request reviewers after substantive updates so they re-check changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcing required reviews (protected branches)
rubrics_metrics.description: Repository administrators can require approvals before pull requests are merged, ensuring code quality and preventing accidental merges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use branch protection rules (About protected branches) to require one or more approvals. This is a procedural control to enforce that reviews happen and that merges meet repository policy.
